Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · House layout, roofs, rooms & furnishings

cell noun

a small room, as in a prison

also prison cell, cells

classical

Ter. Ad. 552
Traupman 124, 372 (small room)

cella, cellae f.

noun, first declension

a small room; a cell

Any small room: a store-room, a porter’s lodge, a slave’s room, a poor man’s garret (Lewis & Short). Varro derives it, rightly, from cēlāre, to hide (LL 5.162).

Other words

  • cellula, cellulae f. — a little room, a small cell

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 309: in cellulam ad tē patris penum omnem congerēbam; Levi–Bini p. 60

    Levi–Bini’s solitary confinement is sēgregātiō in cellulā.

Examples

  • Nam mē jam in cellam aliquam cum illā conclūdam: id tūtissimum est.

    I’ll shut myself up with her in some little room right now: that’s safest.Ter. Ad. 552

See also room, cell, police station.

SourcesLewis & Short: cella · Lewis & Short: cellula
